# Errors {#sec-errors}

Every C call that acts or can fail returns a status of type `BIYOS_status`, an `int`: `BIYOS_OK`, which is zero, or a negative error code. On failure the call keeps a message on its environment that says what went wrong, and changes nothing. No call lets an exception out. The code of this chapter is `examples/c/errors.c` and `examples/python/errors.py`.

## Codes and who is at fault {#sec-errors-codes}

The hundreds of an error code say who is at fault:

| Codes | At fault | Today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| −100 to −199 | the caller | `BIYOS_ERR_BADARG`, −100 |
| −200 to −299 | the model | none yet |
| −300 to −399 | user code, such as a callback | none yet |
| −400 to −499 | resources | `BIYOS_ERR_NOMEMORY`, −400 |
| −500 to −599 | biyos itself | `BIYOS_ERR_INTERNAL`, −500 |

A new code joins its group and keeps its number for good, so test a group by range rather than by value:

```{.c file="examples/c/errors.c" item="at_fault"}
```

Besides the codes the reference names for a call, any call can return `BIYOS_ERR_NOMEMORY` when an allocation fails and `BIYOS_ERR_INTERNAL` on a fault in biyos. No call returns a positive status. A solve outcome, such as an infeasible model or a time limit reached, is never an error code: it is a result, and a call that finds it succeeds.

## The message {#sec-errors-message}

`BIYOS_lasterror` reads the status, the model and the message of the last call on an environment that failed. A call on a model keeps its message on the environment the model was made on.

```{.c file="examples/c/errors.c" item="report"}
```

The message starts with the kind of failure, `invalid argument`, `out of memory` or `internal error`, then says what was wrong:

```text
-100, at fault the caller, on a model: invalid argument: variable 0: bounds [0, 2] are outside [0, 1], the widest of its kind
-100, at fault the caller, on the environment: invalid argument: option 'seed': -1 is outside [0, 2147483647]
```

It is written for people: branch on the status, not on the text. The pointer is never null. It stays valid until the next failed call on the environment or until the environment is freed, and a successful call leaves the message in place. A call given a null environment or model keeps no message, since it has nowhere to keep one, and neither does `BIYOS_newenv`, nor the formatting calls, which take no environment.

## What a failure leaves {#sec-errors-state}

A call that fails changes nothing: no variable is half added, no option half set. It leaves its output arguments as they were, except where its entry in the reference says otherwise; `BIYOS_newenv`, `BIYOS_newmdl` and `BIYOS_copymdl` set their output to null. A null pointer argument gives `BIYOS_ERR_BADARG`, unless the reference says a null is allowed. The example checks that the refused seed left the option at its default:

```{.c file="examples/c/errors.c" item="main"}
```

A failed call also sends an error message on the event stream (@sec-events-sent), so a program can log every failure in one place.

## Errors in Python {#sec-errors-python}

The Python package turns a failed status into a `biyos.Error`, whose `code` holds the status and whose text is the message. Mistakes Python can see by itself raise Python's own exceptions before C is called: `TypeError` for a value of the wrong type, `ValueError` for an array of the wrong length or a closed model, `OverflowError` for an integer that does not fit in 32 bits, `IndexError` for a position outside a block.

```{.python file="examples/python/errors.py"}
```
